subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the supported contract be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into the broader egress policy work?
rationale: This changes an SSRF boundary and public config contract; the lower-level primitive exists, but policy shape, authorization, metadata/link-local handling, redirects, cache isolation, and audit behavior require maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Approve a nested dangerous SSRF policy
options.body: Use a default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` shape that composes with existing fake-IP flags and documents hard-deny, redirect, cache, and provider behavior.

options.title: Keep current narrow fake-IP support only
options.body: Leave arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` unsupported for now and document that internal targets require a trusted proxy, browser policy, or separate owner-approved path.

options.title: Fold into broader egress design
options.body: Make this part of the larger web-tool egress firewall decision so private-network access, allowlists, deny rules, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve a nested dangerous SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Use a default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` shape that composes with existing fake-IP flags and documents hard-deny, redirect, cache, and provider behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They directly commented on the security-sensitive config decision and have the strongest adjacent SSRF/guarded-fetch history in the inspected evidence.
